messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?
Thanks. What matters most is getting a fair financial share; I won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. I haven’t agreed to it. Yes, contact A and B.
We’d like a home of our own, and buying it at a family discount would be more manageable for us. But I know C hasn’t agreed, so nothing can move forward yet.
Thank you. I’d like to have some money to start a dance studio; that matters a lot to me. I’m not sure what’s fair regarding the house or the estate yet, and I don’t want to rush into an agreement.
That fits, though the will and house value aren’t settled yet. I’m fine with accurate shared information and a fair process.
That’s mostly right. Having a home we can afford matters most; the family connection matters too. I’m comfortable with accurate shared information and a fair process.
Yes, those fit. I’m comfortable with accurate shared information and a process we can trust; I’d just like time to understand it all before agreeing.
Option 3’s six-month deadline makes me uncomfortable. I’d like this settled, but there’s no real urgency; I’m not agreeing to a deadline yet.
I’m not sure Option 1 would be affordable; financing B’s and C’s shares could be too much without a family discount. I’d need to see the appraisal and numbers before judging.
I don’t have a firm date in mind, but knowing when my share might be available would help me plan the studio. I’m not ready to choose an option yet.
Yes, I’m OK with confirming the will and getting an independent appraisal. No discomfort with that.
